reason: While this passage from Exodus 14 does include the Israelites complaining to Moses and Moses instructing them to trust God, this is not the primary moral of the narrative. The story's central themes are divine power and miraculous deliverance—God parting the sea and destroying the Egyptian army. The complaints serve as a narrative device to show human fear in crisis, but the text emphasizes faith in God's salvation, not the propriety of whether people should address grievances to leaders. Moses redirects the people's anxiety toward trust in God (אַל־ תִּירָאוּ הִתְיַצְבוּ וּרְאוּ אֶת־ יְשׁוּעַת יְהוָה), and God's subsequent intervention validates this faith. The core lesson concerns God's intervention for His people, not complaint restrictions.
